claims.title: Shopper order data may be readable on the public-to-storefront path
claims.description: `flow:entity:shopper>process:storefront-api>place-order` crosses from the public internet to `process:storefront-api` and carries order contents, shipping addresses, and card last-four data. Its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If transport protection is not enforced end to end, an attacker able to observe this public-facing path can intercept shoppers' PII and financial order data before it reaches the storefront. The disclosed addresses and order details enable targeted fraud and identification of specific orders handled by downstream `process:order-service`. This is conditional on the unresolved transport-encryption attribute, not an assertion that the flow is plaintext.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `flow:entity:shopper>process:storefront-api>place-order` crosses a public trust boundary, but interception still requires an on-path position and the unknown transport control may be present. Impact is high because the flow carries both `pii` and `financial` data, including shipping addresses and card last-four, for shopper orders.

mitigations.summary: Verify and require TLS for shopper order submission
mitigations.detail: Set and enforce strong TLS for `flow:entity:shopper>process:storefront-api>place-order`, including certificate validation and HTTPS-only handling from the shopper to `process:storefront-api`.

mitigations.summary: Minimize payment-related fields in the request
mitigations.detail: Avoid carrying payment-related values unless required by `process:storefront-api`; use opaque payment references where the order workflow can support them.

claims.title: Settlement callback contents may be exposed in transit from the card processor
claims.description: `flow:entity:card-processor>process:storefront-api>settlement-webhook` crosses from the public internet to `process:storefront-api`, carries financial settlement confirmations, and has unknown protocol and `encryption_in_transit` attributes. If the processor callback is not protected by verified transport encryption, an on-path observer can intercept payment-settlement information as it enters the storefront. Those observations reveal which orders were paid and can be correlated with order processing in `process:order-service`; the threat is conditional on the unresolved transport posture.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `flow:entity:card-processor>process:storefront-api>settlement-webhook` is a public-boundary crossing, though the attacker must obtain an on-path position and the unknown encryption control may be present. Impact is medium because the flow is tagged `financial` and exposes settlement status, but the model describes a settlement confirmation rather than the complete order corpus.

mitigations.summary: Require verified TLS for processor callbacks
mitigations.detail: Document and enforce TLS with certificate validation for `flow:entity:card-processor>process:storefront-api>settlement-webhook`; reject callbacks received without the required protected transport.

mitigations.summary: Limit callback data to an opaque settlement reference
mitigations.detail: Have the callback carry only the minimum opaque order or settlement reference needed by `process:storefront-api`, resolving further details internally.

claims.title: Order details may be intercepted between the storefront and order service
claims.description: `flow:process:storefront-api>process:order-service>submit-order` crosses from `boundary:storefront-dmz` into `boundary:core-services` and carries shopper identifiers, shipping addresses, and order contents tagged `pii` and `financial`. Its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If this gRPC transport is not encrypted, an attacker able to observe the DMZ-to-core path can intercept submitted order data without accessing either endpoint. The collected identifiers and order details enable targeted attacks against affected shoppers and correlation with records subsequently persisted in `store:orders-db`. This is conditional on the unverified encryption state.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional: `flow:process:storefront-api>process:order-service>submit-order` crosses into the core-services zone, so an attacker needs a position on that internal path, while its encryption state is unknown. Impact is high because the flow carries `pii` and `financial` order data for every submitted order, including shopper identifiers and shipping addresses.

mitigations.summary: Use mTLS on the storefront-to-order-service gRPC call
mitigations.detail: Require TLS 1.2+ with mutual authentication on `flow:process:storefront-api>process:order-service>submit-order` so order payloads remain confidential across the DMZ-to-core boundary.

mitigations.summary: Reduce sensitive fields on the service hop
mitigations.detail: Pass an opaque order reference where possible and let `process:order-service` resolve sensitive fields from its authorized storage path.

claims.title: Order database traffic may expose shopper records to an internal path observer
claims.description: `flow:process:order-service>store:orders-db>read-write-orders` reads and writes `store:orders-db` records containing shipping addresses and card last-four data, and its `protocol` and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the database connection is not encrypted, an attacker with an observation position in `boundary:core-services` can intercept order rows in transit between `process:order-service` and `store:orders-db`. The captured records expose confidential PII and financial data and enable targeting of shoppers whose orders the service processes. This is conditional on the unresolved protocol and transport-encryption facts; it does not assert that the database connection is cleartext.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because observing `flow:process:order-service>store:orders-db>read-write-orders` requires an internal core-services network foothold, and its transport protection is unknown rather than stated absent. Impact is high because `store:orders-db` is confidential and tagged `pii` and `financial`, while the flow carries full order rows, addresses, and card last-four values.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and authenticate the database connection
mitigations.detail: Require TLS for `flow:process:order-service>store:orders-db>read-write-orders`, validate the database certificate, and use mutually authenticated or workload-bound database access where supported.
Segment the database connection path and permit only `process:order-service` to reach the database listener, reducing opportunities for packet capture within the core-services zone.

claims.title: A storage copy could reveal all orders if orders-db encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:orders-db` is classified confidential and holds `pii` and `financial` data, including shopper addresses and card last-four values, but `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If that unknown resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker who obtains a decommissioned volume, snapshot, backup, or other operational copy of this PostgreSQL store can read the order corpus without using the normal application authentication path. The resulting corpus disclosure enables targeting of every shopper represented in the database and persists even after the copied media is recovered. This threat is conditional on the unresolved at-rest encryption attribute, not a claim that encryption is absent.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:orders-db` has an unknown `encryption_at_rest` state and obtaining an operational storage copy avoids application-level access controls. Impact is high because `store:orders-db` is classified confidential and tagged `pii` and `financial`, so one raw copy exposes the order corpus, shopper addresses, and payment-related values.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encryption at rest for orders-db and its copies
mitigations.detail: Establish the `encryption_at_rest` posture of `store:orders-db`, then require managed-key or customer-managed-key encryption for the primary database and every backup, snapshot, replica, and export.

mitigations.summary: Constrain access to storage copies and keys
mitigations.detail: Use separate, least-privilege roles for backup, export, and key-use operations, and audit or alert on snapshot and backup retrieval.

claims.title: A database password recovered from the order-service environment can expose all orders
claims.description: The application-account password used by `flow:process:order-service>store:orders-db>read-write-orders` is kept in an environment variable on `process:order-service`, and that account has full read/write access to `store:orders-db`. An attacker who recovers that credential from the worker environment can authenticate as the application account and read the confidential order corpus, including shopper addresses and card last-four values, rather than being limited to an individual order. Second-order, the stolen password also lets the attacker appear as the order service when querying the database, making the disclosure path harder to distinguish from normal service access.

quotes.text: The password comes from an environment variable on the worker.
a single application account that has full read/write

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because the password is a static application credential held in an environment variable on `process:order-service`, though the attacker must first obtain access sufficient to recover it. Impact is high because the application account has stated full read/write access to confidential `store:orders-db`, which holds `pii` and `financial` order records.

mitigations.summary: Replace the environment-held static password with short-lived credentials
mitigations.detail: Use workload identity or short-lived database credentials issued through a dedicated secret-management system rather than retaining the application-account password in the `process:order-service` environment.

mitigations.summary: Reduce the application account's database read scope
mitigations.detail: Replace the full read/write grant with narrowly scoped roles, tables, columns, and operations needed by `process:order-service`, and monitor for corpus-scale reads.
